messages:
incident-bot: Pager: P0 — inference-prod queue depth high for the past 12m. queue_length=18,432 avg_wait=23.2s autoscaler_error_count=312
ryan (on-call): ack. jumping in. seeing throttles on gpu-pool-east-1 and a bunch of 429s surfaced in the proxy logs.
maya (sre): joining. any known deploys? services?
ryan (on-call): no deploys on prod since midnight. traffic steady-ish. looks like queue growth triggered scale but scale requests kept failing.
jun (infra): pulling autoscaler logs. interesting: repeated failures with `placement failed: no node matches MIG request` and `allocation rejected: insufficient slice types`. also many nodes have leftover small MIG slices that aren't being reused — fragmentation.
jun (infra): snippet from autoscaler: ```2026-02-15T14:02:11Z ERROR scale_up failed request_id=abc123 reason=placement_failed details="requested_mig=vgpu_1g.5gb available_types=[1g.10gb,2g.20gb]"```
sam (runtime): that matches an earlier change where we started preferring strict MIG matches for better perf. if workloads request 1g.5gb but nodes only expose 1g.10gb instances (different slice naming) scheduler rejects; results in stranded capacity.
anna (cs): multiple customers reporting spike in inference latency and some 429s. Acme reported a 3x increase in avg response time and BetaCorp says some requests queued > 30s. posting interim notice. :warning:
anna (cs): message to affected customers: "We're investigating an issue causing elevated inference latency in us-east. Our on-call is actively mitigating; we'll update w/ ETA in 15m"
ryan (on-call): current status: queue 18k, running pods 380, autoscaler at max_replicas=50 (policy), scale attempts=122. autoscaler is hitting placement failures so adding nodes doesn't help.
maya (sre): can we temporarily bump max_replicas? Jun, what are the quota/cost constraints?
jun (infra): cloud quota allows up to 80 for emergency but need an infra-owner ack — I'm ok to authorize 80 for 2h. cost team notified. do we expect that to help?
sam (runtime): not until we address binpacking/fragmentation. If new nodes come up with mixed MIG flavors we might still have the same mismatch. We need either 1) relax strict-mig matching in scheduler to allow fallback, or 2) force a rebalance to consolidate smaller slices.
ryan (on-call): plan: (A) increase max_replicas -> 80 (emergency, 2h) (B) apply runtime hotfix to allow 'best-effort' placement for compatible MIGs (C) manual rebalance / drain a few nodes to free consistent slices (D) customer comms.
jun (infra): executing (A) now: `PATCH /autoscaler/policy max_replicas=80 emergency=true` — response OK.
devops-bot: autoscaler policy patched by jun. new max_replicas=80 (effective now).
ryan (on-call): triggering scale. if we see new machines fail allocation, we go to step B.
sam (runtime): creating PR for relaxed placement: will allow matching on capacity instead of exact MIG name when `best_effort=true`. small perf delta but should restore throughput. deploying as hotfix in canary then prod.
sam (runtime): deploy started to prod canary group (10%): `deploy/runtime-hotfix#451`
devops-bot: deploy/runtime-hotfix#451 started by sam. canary: 38 pods. health: passing.
sam (runtime): canary looks good. rolling to remainder. this should allow allocator to pack 1g.5gb workloads onto 1g.10gb slices if free capacity exists.
jun (infra): I'm starting a manual drain on node-az-east-12 to consolidate the smaller slices onto node-az-east-05 — hoping to reduce fragmentation. draining 1 node at a time to avoid extra disruption.
maya (sre): monitoring queue after hotfix and drain.
~8m later~
ryan (on-call): queue dropped from 18,432 to 4,100 in ~12m since hotfix and manual rebalance. avg_wait down to 6.8s. autoscaler pushed to 68 replicas to catch up.
anna (cs): updated customers: "We deployed a targeted mitigation; latency is improving. We'll keep monitoring and follow up with root cause and timeline for permanent fix." :thumbsup:
sam (runtime): runtime hotfix committed & rolled back only if we see regressions. no regressions in perf traces so far.
jun (infra): manual rebalance freed ~9k worth of slice capacity (est). I left a note to schedule a full defrag job overnight to compact MIGs across the fleet.
maya (sre): current status: reduced severity to P1; still monitoring for 1h. need postmortem.
ryan (on-call): handoff to maya for 4h watch. I'll update incident log and create the follow-up action items: - autoscaler: add placement fallback policy - nightly defrag: schedule automated MIG packer - eval: change default MIG request to be more flexible - cost: emergency quota doc
maya (sre): ack. I'm taking over. summary for postmortem: root cause = strict MIG-matching + binpacking fragmentation -> stranded capacity -> autoscaler hit scale cap and placement failures -> queue growth and customer latency. mitigation = emergency scale + scheduler best-effort + manual rebalance. next steps = schedule defrag job, add canary for placement policy, update runbook.
anna (cs): will coordinate customer follow-ups once postmortem is ready.
ryan (on-call): thanks team. logging final notes and timeline in incident tracker. closing thread for active paging; monitoring channel will remain open.
incident-bot: Incident update recorded. Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. incident_id=INC-2026-0215-01" 
}
